caption:
I’m still learning… that every person you meet carries a key. Not to complete you, but to unlock unexplored parts of yourself you hadn’t met yet. Some connections may not last, but the versions of you they awaken do.

words & wisdom by afsarosette
author: رغدان
transcript: what I wish I knew about dating. Don't date to find a partner. Date to study your reactions. To see where you abandon yourself and who you become when you're uncertain. Date to observe how much silence you can tolerate before you start performing for reassurance. Dating is one of the deepest spiritual mirrors if you let it be. Because not every person who knocks on your door has the capacity to come inside and help you build. Some just want shelter for the night or a distraction or just a good time. Your job is to know yourself so fucking well that you can enjoy a conversation without constructing a future. Yes, some people waste other people's time but also some people keep trying to make time mean something. Every conversation doesn't need to lead somewhere. We suffer because we skip the stage of witnessing and go straight into wanting. So the work isn't just date better people. The work is learning to differentiate between ease and escape.
title: Date to Know Yourself, Not Find Someone
one_liner: Use dating as a mirror to study your reactions and patterns rather than seeking a partner.
key_points: Date to observe where you abandon yourself, not to find a relationship
Not everyone who enters your life has capacity to build with you — discern shelter-seekers from builders
Suffering comes from skipping the witnessing stage and jumping straight into wanting
The real work is distinguishing between genuine ease and emotional escape
